metadata.title: Special Stable Matrices and Their Non-square Counterpart

nodes.name: Sufficient DUS Condition for Non-Square Systems
assumptions: For a proper and asymptotically stable non-square system $H(s) \in \mathbb{C}^{m \times n}$, with steady state transfer matrix $A=H(0) \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times m}$, if there exists a block diagonal non-square matrix $K \in \mathbb{C}^{n \times m}$ such that for all non-negative diagonal matrices $E \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$, and $j \in \mathcal{M}$, $Re\{ \sigma_i ( [A E K]_j ) \} >0$
conclusions: Then the nonsquare system can be controlled by a distributed integral controller and achieve Decentralized Unconditional Stability.
nodes.label: theorem1

nodes.name: Volterra-Lyapunov Stability Implies D-Stability
assumptions: If a matrix $A=(a_{ij}) \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$ is Volterra-Lyapunov stable
conclusions: Then, for any diagonal positive matrix $D > 0$ and $i \in \mathcal{M}$, $Re\{ \sigma [AD]_i \} >0$, which implies that $[A]_i$, for $i \in \mathcal{M}$, are all D-stable matrices.
nodes.label: lemma2

nodes.name: Card Combination Payoff Lemma
assumptions: Consider $m$ groups of cards, where each group contains $p_i$ distinct cards. A player can place a bet on each combination of $m$ cards, one card from each group. The payoff for a specific combination is denoted as $\gamma(\zeta_1, \zeta_2, \cdots, \zeta_m) > 0$. Suppose the player desires a specific ratio $\kappa_{kj} > 0$ between the $j_{th}$ card of group $k$ and the first card of that group.
conclusions: If the set of payoffs $\gamma(\zeta_1, \zeta_2, \cdots, \zeta_m)$ satisfies the conditions in equation (\ref{sub_sssa}), then the player can implement their desired strategy.
nodes.label: pailiezuhe_Lemma

nodes.name: Simultaneous Volterra-Lyapunov Stability Implies Non-Square D-Stability
assumptions: If a real nonsquare matrix $A \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n}$ is a simultaneous Volterra-Lyapunov stable matrix (see Definition \ref{def_NSQ_lyp})
conclusions: Then, there exists a block diagonal non-square matrix $K \in \mathbb{C}^{n \times m}$ such that for all non-negative diagonal matrices $E \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$, and $j \in \mathcal{M}$, $Re\{ \sigma_i ( [A E K]_j ) \} >0$.
nodes.label: simul_lemma22a

nodes.name: Equivalence for Normal Matrices in Class F
assumptions: For normal matrices and in the class $\mathbb{F} = \{A : a_{ij} \ge 0 \,\,for \,\,all \,\, i \ne j \}$
conclusions: D-stability and Volterra-Lyapunov stability are all equivalent to stability.
nodes.label: lem2

nodes.name: Equivalence of Stability Notions for Sets of Normal Matrices in Class F
assumptions: For a set of normal matrices which are also in the class $\mathbb{F} = \{A : a_{ij} \ge 0 \,\,for \,\,all \,\, i \ne j \}$
conclusions: D-stability, individual Volterra-Lyapunov stability, and simultaneous Volterra-Lyapunov stability are all equivalent to stability.
nodes.label: lem33

nodes.name: D-stability of Normal Matrices in Class F for Non-Square Matrices
assumptions: If any of the $m_{th}$-order squared matrices of $A \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n}$ is a normal matrix and in the class $\mathbb{F}$, and also D-stable matrix
conclusions: Then there exists a block diagonal non-square matrix $K \in \mathbb{C}^{n \times m}$ such that for all non-negative diagonal matrices $E \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$, and $j \in \mathcal{M}$, $Re\{ \sigma_i ( [A E K]_j ) \} >0$.
nodes.label: mainreslt

nodes.name: Individual Volterra-Lyapunov Stability Implies Non-Square D-Stability
assumptions: A real nonsquare matrix $A \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n}$ is an individual Volterra-Lyapunov stable matrix (see Definition \ref{def_NSQ_lyp_ind})
conclusions: There exists a block diagonal non-square matrix $K \in \mathbb{C}^{n \times m}$ such that for all non-negative diagonal matrices $E \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$, and $j \in \mathcal{M}$, where $\mathcal{M}$ is the index set consisting of $k$ tuples of integers in the range $1,\cdots, m$, $Re\{ \sigma_i ( [A E K]_j ) \} >0$, where $\text{Re} \{ \sigma_i (M) \}$ represents the real part of the $i$-th eigenvalue of matrix $M$.

nodes.name: Conjecture on Individual Volterra-Lyapunov Stable Non-Square Matrices
assumptions: A real nonsquare matrix $A \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n}$ is an individual Volterra-Lyapunov stable matrix, meaning one can find an individual diagonal positive matrix $D_i > 0$ so that all its $m$-order squared matrices $[A]^m_{s_i}$ satisfy $[A]^m_{s_i} D_i + D_i ([A]^m_{s_i})^T > 0$.
conclusions: Conjecture that if a real nonsquare matrix is individual Volterra-Lyapunov stable, then there exists a block diagonal non-square matrix $K$ such that for all non-negative diagonal matrices $E$ and all index tuples $j \in \mathcal{M}$, the real parts of all eigenvalues of $[AEK]_j$ are positive.
